_comment: Which scorer each lane invokes, and how.  Edited by hand when an engine's
CLI changes; read by bin/fidelity/engines.py.  A lane with pinned:false
refuses to plan -- see the module docstring for why guessing flags is worse
Verify a lane after editing:  bin/measure-local --probe-engines

sealed-ep8.name: k6_student_capture + k6_kld_report (sealed EP8 lane)

timing.provenance: ESTIMATE, NOT MEASURED. No per-window wall clock was recorded for the sealed EP8 lane in a form this runner can cite. The figure is a deliberately conservative placeholder so the cost estimate errs high rather than low; the max-runtime coherence check uses it, and the printed estimate labels it. Replace it with a measured number from a sealed-lane run receipt.

notes: This is the lane K6 and Q4 were measured with, and the only one whose
flags are verified against the file in this checkout.  EP size is
env-driven (QP_GLM53_EP_SIZE) and the launcher's --nproc-per-node must
match it.  Requires the patched quant_pipeline tree (--pipeline-root)
and a BF16 skeleton carrying config.json + model.safetensors.index.json,
because the capture binds inventory.config_sha256/index_sha256 to the
LOCAL files.
--surface packed dereferences packed_root from the checkpoint's own
materialization-receipt.json.  For a third-party artifact that path is
on the producer's machine; see hfmeta.sniff_surface, which detects this
before any money is spent.

streaming.name: stream_score (single-GPU streaming lane)
streaming.unpinned_reason: k6/tools/stream_score.py is not present in this checkout. It was built and validated on the streaming-validation box and has not been synced back. Its flags are therefore UNKNOWN, and this file will not guess them.
contract: --checkpoint PATH        the artifact to score
--panel PATH             the fetched teacher/panel directory
--out PATH               receipts + tokenwise-kld output root
--surface NAME           packed | dione | tr3-published
--reduce-order {fp32,native}   fp32 is the validated setting: the
window-0 KLD delta vs the sealed EP8 lane is
+1.5076e-5 at 99.80% argmax agreement
--cold-run N             labels the capture receipt
--roles final            which panel roles to score
it must emit a tokenwise-KLD tensor whose sha256 is the determinism
evidence (NOT a receipt-file hash -- see registry DET-001)
notes: Known properties from the validation run, which the receipt must
disclose: bitwise cross-topology parity is impossible (routed-expert
combine order moves logits rms 0.26-0.28); streaming runs ARE bitwise
identical to each other, so determinism holds WITHIN the lane; peak
34-47 GB on one H200 as currently scheduled.

timing.provenance: MEASURED: the streaming validation reported ~$0.30/window on one H200 at $1.99/GPU-h, which is 0.1508 h = 9.05 min/window, and ~$7.50 for a 25-window panel.

local-mps.name: stream_score on Apple Silicon (MPS)
local-mps.unpinned_reason: Same missing file as the streaming lane, plus two Apple-Silicon constraints that must be honoured by whatever lands: MPS cannot do float64 AT ALL (not slowly -- torch raises TypeError), so the KLD accumulation must run on CPU; and 34 of 45 layers are Kimi-Delta linear attention whose only known fast paths are Triton/CUDA or a fused MLX kernel, so the torch/MPS forward is UNVERIFIED.
contract: everything the streaming lane requires, plus:
--device {auto,mps,cuda,cpu}
--kld-device cpu         MANDATORY on MPS. estimator.accumulation_dtype
is a comparability key input, so silently
degrading fp64 to fp32 would move the row into
a different comparability group. Refuse, do
not degrade.
--expert-chunk N         numerics-invariant memory knob
--window-batch N         numerics-invariant memory knob
--vram-budget GB         honoured as a hard bound
notes: Measured on a 128 GB M4 Max: the EXL3/TR3 decode is pure PyTorch (no
custom kernel, no exllamav3 build) and is BITWISE IDENTICAL on MPS and
CPU at both 4 and 6 bits, over full-size 8,388,608-element matrices.
So the local lanes carry NO device offset from weight decode; any
local-vs-sealed offset comes from the forward pass alone.
Consequence for the recipe: `pip install torch safetensors numpy
huggingface_hub` is sufficient locally. None of stage_k6.sh's
bootstrap (deadsnakes, CUDA 13, flash-attn, exllamav3) is needed.

timing.provenance: DERIVED from measured per-matrix decode on a 128 GB M4 Max (16.7 ms/matrix at 6 bits, 14.0 ms at 4 bits, MPS, int32 unpack) under the panel-batched layer-outer schedule, where the 36,288-matrix routed pass happens ONCE for the whole panel rather than once per window. That makes per-window time an amortisation, not a measurement: ~15 min for the whole 25-window panel. The forward pass itself (KDA/DSA/mHC on MPS) is UNVERIFIED and is not in this figure.

local-cuda-budget.name: stream_score under a VRAM budget (consumer CUDA)
local-cuda-budget.unpinned_reason: Same missing file as the streaming lane.
contract: everything the streaming lane requires, plus:
--vram-budget GB         hard bound, honoured not approximated
--expert-chunk N         numerics-invariant
--window-batch N         numerics-invariant
--nonrouted-residency {pinned,mmap,gpu}
the scatter-add over experts MUST be sequential in ascending expert
order. An atomicAdd-based scatter would make the result depend on the
memory knobs, which destroys the invariance the recipe promises.
notes: Peak for the panel-batched layer-outer schedule on GLM-5.3-Flash at
4bpw: 23.5 GB whole-layer, 25.5 GB at the solver's default fill for a
30 GB budget. The floor for ANY schedule is 4.6 GB, set by the lm_head
weight plus one window of fp32 logits -- neither shrinks with the
memory knobs.

timing.provenance: PROJECTED. No Blackwell hardware was available. Scales the measured Apple-Silicon decode by memory bandwidth (1.79 TB/s vs ~410-546 GB/s) and treats the run as I/O-bound on reading 176-254 GB once. Treat as an order-of-magnitude figure until someone runs it.
